A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SpeciaRL study. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including material relocated between the main text and supplement.

before.justification: V1 reports original classification experiments, training ablations, qualitative examples, and judge-validation results in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: V3 retains these original empirical results, including the in-domain evaluation and optimizer comparisons moved into the appendix.

M1.justification: The prediction categorization, adaptive specificity threshold, binary reward, and online rollout procedure remain unchanged in Equations (1)–(11). Revised descriptions of optimizer compatibility do not change the algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions use CUB, Flowers102, Food101, OxfordPets, FGVCAircraft, and StanfordCars, retaining the same in-domain, out-of-domain, and mixed-domain coverage. Moving the CUB evaluation into the appendix adds no new scenario.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged across the corresponding experiments, including retrieval methods, LMMs, prompting variants, SFT, RFT, and BoN-64. Dr.GRPO and DAPO already appear in v1 Table 6 and are retained in v3 Table 13.

E3.justification: The reported training budgets, model configurations, prompts, metrics, and experimental controls are unchanged. Added caption details clarify existing evaluations without reporting a changed split or procedure.

E4.justification: Both retain the reward, rollout-count, training-domain, training-size, mixed-domain, optimizer, judge-agreement, and injected-noise analyses, plus the same qualitative failure cases. The optimizer analysis is relocated rather than added.

E5.justification: Agreement-rate and Cohen's kappa reporting remain unchanged. Neither version adds repeated-run counts, seed information, confidence intervals, or significance testing.

E6.justification: Corresponding numerical results and qualitative examples are unchanged. For example, Table 1 retains SpeciaRL HM values of 0.883 and 0.830; the CUB and optimizer results remain identical after moving from v1 Tables 3 and 6 to v3 Tables 7 and 13.

T1.justification: The category ordering, metric definitions, Best-of-N definition, and reward equations retain the same mathematical content. No theorem, proof, assumption, or derivation is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract and contribution list retain the same claims about prior knowledge, dynamic rewards, and the specificity–correctness trade-off. The conclusion's GRPO-compatible wording clarifies applicability already supported by v1's multiple-optimizer analysis.

C2.justification: V3 Section B.2 adds the interpretation that fine-tuning acquires domain-specific information as well as changing classification behavior. Its following statement that this 'does hinder generalization' conflicts with the strong out-of-domain performance invoked as support. Existing failure-case interpretations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: V3 Table 10 explicitly identifies the CUB test set for the training-size ablation, and Table 15 specifies averaging over fine-grained datasets. These are limited reporting clarifications; prompts, hyperparameters, hardware, runtime information, and code/model access statements remain unchanged.

R1.justification: V3 adds formal references for the already-evaluated Dr.GRPO and DAPO algorithms. Section 2 also describes SpeciaRL as compatible with on-policy optimizers rather than as extending GRPO, while retaining the broader research positioning.

P1.justification: V3 moves the in-domain and optimizer discussions into dedicated appendix subsections, condenses the ablation overview, and makes localized wording and acknowledgement edits. Most prose and the overall narrative structure are retained.

P2.justification: The in-domain and optimizer tables move from the main text to the appendix, with corresponding renumbering and page reflow. Several captions are clarified and Figure 4 changes column placement; the substantive figure and table contents are retained.

improvement.justification: V3 modestly improves methodological clarity, attribution, and reporting through more precise optimizer-compatibility wording, added optimizer references, and clearer evaluation captions, while retaining all empirical evidence. These gains are partly offset by the contradictory new 'does hinder generalization' sentence in Section B.2.
